subject: mathematics
question_text: If sin θ = −1/3 and θ does not lie in the third quadrant, find the value of (i) cos θ (ii) cot θ.

mark_split.label: Find cos θ and cot θ

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.106 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 163. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed VSAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: TS 19. The quadrant clause is the whole question. sin θ is negative in the third and fourth quadrants; ruling out the third leaves the fourth, where cos θ is positive. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Fix the quadrant
steps.margin_note: First mark. sin θ negative means Q3 or Q4. The question rules out Q3, so θ is in Q4 — and cos θ is positive there.
steps.memory_tip: sin negative means Q3 or Q4; Q3 is ruled out, so Q4 — where cos is POSITIVE.
lines: sin θ is negative in Q₃ and Q₄.
Since θ is not in Q₃, θ lies in Q₄.
In Q₄, cos θ is positive.

recall.must_convey: That sin θ negative gives Q3 or Q4, the clause rules out Q3, so θ is in Q4 where cos θ is positive.
accept: sine is negative in the third and fourth quadrants and the third is ruled out so theta is in the fourth where cosine is positive
the quadrant decides the sign of the cosine
theta lies in the fourth quadrant so cos theta is positive
Q three ruled out kabatti Q four, akkada cos positive
fix the quadrant before taking the square root

steps.why: The square root that follows has two signs. The quadrant is the only thing that chooses between them, so it has to be settled first.
common_mistakes: Ignoring the quadrant clause entirely and writing ±.

steps.label: Find cos θ and cot θ
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Use cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ with the positive root, then cot θ = cos θ / sin θ. The 1/3 cancels.
steps.memory_tip: Take the positive root, then cot = cos/sin. The thirds cancel, leaving −√8.
lines: (ii) cot θ = cos θ / sin θ = (√8/3)/(−1/3)

recall.must_convey: That cos θ = √8/3 and cot θ = cos θ/sin θ = −√8.
accept: cos theta is root eight over three and cot theta is minus root eight
one minus one ninth is eight ninths so the cosine is root eight by three
the thirds cancel in the cotangent leaving minus root eight
cos theta root eight by three, cot theta minus root eight

steps.why: Both denominators are 3, so they cancel in the ratio. cot θ comes out as a whole surd with no fraction left.
common_mistakes: Leaving cot θ as a fraction with 3s still in it.
